CROWD MANAGEMENT PLAN
St. Anne's Sunset Run Half Marathon, Sunday 28 November 2027
Applicant: St. Anne's Parish Fun Run Committee
Prepared by Patrick Doyle, Race Director
Issue: 3.0

1. Attendance
We expect 650 people in total at the event, including 430 runners. About 220 of those are spectators.

Families are welcome, and there is usually a friendly atmosphere at the finish. Local shops have been supportive, and some stay open for the day. The prize-giving takes place at the end, and there is often a queue for tea.

2. Spectator areas
Spectators will be directed to three marked viewing areas behind pedestrian barriers: the finish area by the Civic Plaza, the turn at Orchard Road and the start at the top of Union Row. Together these hold approximately 850 people at a planning density of two persons per square metre, which exceeds the expected attendance.

3. Start procedure
All entrants will assemble in the start area shortly before 08:00 and will start together following a short welcome and warm-up led by a local sports personality, which has always proved popular in previous years.

4. Stewarding
13 stewards in high-visibility tabards, led by 2 supervisors, are allocated by position on the attached rota. That is around one steward for every 50 people expected. All attend a briefing at the site one hour before the start.

5. Exit and dispersal
Following the race, participants and their families are welcome to stay and enjoy the prize-giving and refreshments before making their own way home at their leisure. There are good public transport links nearby.

6. Event control
The event controller, Patrick Doyle, sits at the control point with radio contact to all supervisors and can hold a start, stop the race or use the public address to move people. A supervisor reports to the controller if any pen or viewing area appears to be filling beyond its marked capacity.

attachments.name: medical_plan.txt
attachments.text:
Medical cover for the St. Anne's Sunset Run Half Marathon, Sunday 28 November 2027

From Patrick Doyle, Race Director, St. Anne's Parish Fun Run Committee

The race is a half marathon with 430 runners and starts at 08:00. No ambulance will be stationed at the race; any ambulance would come through the 911 system.

First aid
Several of our members have done the first aid course through work, and they're happy to help out. We keep a good first aid box at the HQ tent, and another one goes in the lead car. In all our years we've only ever had blisters and scraped knees.

Heat, cold and water
There's water every 2.5 km. We look at the forecast two days before and again two hours before. Over 28 degrees we start earlier or cut the course, and over 32 degrees we call it off. If it's cold or wet, we have foil blankets and a warm tent at the finish.

If someone needs hospital
The nearest emergency department is at Harbourside Medical Centre, 4 km from the finish. We've walked the route out from the pick-up point at the top of Union Row with the first aiders, and we've told the hospital the date and how many are coming.

Staying in touch
We'll all have our phones, and I'll send a list of numbers round the team the week before. The signal is usually fine around there.

Who's responsible
Our medical lead is Ellis Grant, a registered paramedic, who'll be there from an hour before the start until the last runner is in and has the final word on pulling any runner out.

Some background. Our committee has run this race for a number of years and takes the welfare of runners to heart. One of our longtime members is a retired paramedic who usually runs the race herself and is not on duty that day.

attachments.name: race_plan.txt
attachments.text:
RACE PLAN
St. Anne's Sunset Run Half Marathon | Sunday 28 November 2027
Organiser: St. Anne's Parish Fun Run Committee
Race director: Patrick Doyle
Reference: EV-68103

Overview
The St. Anne's Sunset Run Half Marathon is a half marathon race of 21 km for 430 entrants, based in the Clocktower Square area of Port Halden. The start is at 08:00 and the course closes at 11:30.

Course
The course runs in order along Union Row, Ash Avenue, Orchard Road and Rope Walk, all of which are closed to traffic for the race. Major roads crossed: High Street, Dock Road and Tram Street. The finish is in the Civic Plaza.

Course dimensions
The course uses wide carriageways throughout. Union Row offers 11 m kerb to kerb, Orchard Road about 9 m and Rope Walk about 14 m, with footways of a further 3 m on each side. The field assembles on Union Row, and the finish is in the Civic Plaza, an open paved area of around one and a half hectares.

Support
Entrants collect numbers from the top of Union Row from one hour before the start. Timing is by chip, with mats at the start and finish. Results are posted on the St. Anne's website the same day.

attachments.name: traffic_plan.txt
attachments.text:
TRAFFIC MANAGEMENT PLAN
Event: St. Anne's Sunset Run Half Marathon
Date: Sunday 28 November 2027
Applicant: St. Anne's Parish Fun Run Committee
Prepared by: Brightway Traffic Consulting
Issue: 3.0

1. Scope
This plan describes how traffic will be managed for the St. Anne's Sunset Run Half Marathon, a half marathon race in the Clocktower Square area of Port Halden with a 08:00 start. It has been prepared to accompany the permit application and should be read with the race plan. Police attendance is covered in the attached correspondence.

2. Road closures
The principal closure will be on Union Row. Elsewhere on the course, traffic will be held dynamically by the appointed contractor as the field passes, in line with accepted industry practice. Signal Hill Traffic Services will confirm the detailed arrangements following a pre-event site visit.

3. Major crossings
Each major crossing has its own control point, staffed from 06:45 until the last runner has passed.
- High Street at Orchard Road: 4 traffic marshals with stop/go boards, one supervisor
- Dock Road at Union Row: 2 traffic marshals with stop/go boards, one supervisor
- Tram Street at Union Row: 3 traffic marshals with stop/go boards, one supervisor

4. Diversions
Drivers will be advised to expect delays in the area and to allow additional time for their journeys. Advance information boards will be used where practical, and through traffic is expected to find alternative routes across the wider network.

5. Emergency vehicle access
The emergency services will be made aware of the event date and general location through the usual channels ahead of the day. Any vehicle attending an incident will be accommodated by staff on the ground as circumstances allow.

6. Notification
All frontages on the closed streets receive a letter drop 21 days before the event, with a further reminder at 7 days. Advance notice signs go up 10 days before, and bus operators have been given the closure times.

7. Reopening
A sweep vehicle follows the last runner. Closures are lifted in the order listed, after a barrier and litter check, with all roads open by 12:00.

Volunteers get a short note about the day in race week, with their start time, and are asked to find a replacement if they cannot make it. Most of them have done this before and know the area well.
